name: Alternate Leg Diagonal Bound
method: Plyometric bounding drill; quality and distance matter, no max-clean-rep norms exist. Prescribe by sets/contacts, not a rep ceiling.
check: Bounding is a plyometric drill scored on distance and quality. Clean-rep norms don't exist, so not_max_test is correct. Keep it prescribed by contacts or sets.

name: Bench Jump
method: Box/bench jump is a power drill; the standard metric is height, not max reps. No rep norms found.
check: Box and bench jumps are power drills measured by height. Rep norms don't exist, so not_max_test is correct.

name: Depth Jump
method: Depth jumps are reactive-strength plyometrics, measured by jump height or reactive strength index with low fixed volume. Rep ceilings are not a meaningful test.
check: Depth jumps are measured by jump height or RSI (reactive strength index), with low fixed volume. A max-rep test would push people into fatigued, unsafe reps, so not_max_test is correct.

name: Knee Tuck Jump
sources: Tuck Jump Assessment protocol (JSSM 2017 / World Rugby) <https://passport.world.rugby/conditioning-for-rugby/advanced-conditioning-for-rugby-pre-level-2/functional-screening-and-dynamic-testing/the-tuck-jump-test>
method: The only standard is the Myer Tuck Jump Assessment, which is a 10 s technique screen scored by deviations. It has no published rep norms or cutoffs.
check: The Tuck Jump Assessment source (World Rugby passport, a plausible and relevant URL) is a 10 s technique screen scored on faults, not on rep count. not_max_test is correct.

name: Rocket Jump
method: Explosive vertical jump; judged by height and landing quality. No max-rep norms.
check: A single-effort explosive jump scored on height and landing. No rep norms exist, so not_max_test is correct.

name: Side Standing Long Jump
method: Distance jump. Measured in cm, not reps.
check: Scored as distance, not reps. not_max_test is correct.

name: Single-Leg Lateral Hop
method: Lateral hop is an agility and landing-control drill. Hop tests in the literature measure distance or time, with no max-clean-rep norms found.
check: Hop tests in the literature use distance or time, such as side-hop counts within a fixed time, not a max clean set. not_max_test is correct.

name: Single-Leg Soft-Landing Holds
method: Balance and landing-control drill. Quality is binary, so a rep ceiling is not meaningful.
check: A landing and balance control drill. A rep ceiling has no meaning here, so not_max_test is correct.

name: Ski hops
method: Time-based plyometric/cardio drill (lateral hops). No hold-seconds norms exist, and effort is set by interval prescription.
check: A timed interval cardio drill with no hold-seconds norms. not_max_test is correct, and the effort is set by interval prescription.

name: Snap Down
method: Landing-mechanics drill from athletic coaching (stance-snap). It is a technique pattern, not a strength test.
check: A drill for landing mechanics, not a strength or endurance test. not_max_test is correct.

name: Standing Long Jump
method: Standing long jump is a fitness test, but it is scored as distance (cm), not reps.
check: A standard fitness test, but it is scored in cm, not reps. not_max_test is correct.

name: Star Jump
sources: Eat This: jumping jacks fitness test <https://www.eatthis.com/jumping-jacks-fitness-test/> ; HuffPost UK: jumping jacks by age <https://huffingtonpost.co.uk/entry/jumping-jack-good-number-by-age_uk_6749907ce4b0918713e2cbae>
method: Searched for star jump and jumping-jack norms. Only popular-press per-minute figures exist (Eat This: intermediate 50-60, advanced 70+ per 60 s; HuffPost/Daily Mail age norms men 25: 60-70). They conflict and measure paced cardio over 60 s, not a max clean single set. Mapping them onto the five tiers would be a guess, so no proposal.
check: The only figures are popular-press jumping-jack counts per 60 s. Eat This and HuffPost UK are real, relevant pages, but they disagree with each other and measure paced cardio, not a max clean set. Declining to map them onto the tiers is defensible. If the app needs a band, it should remain an interval prescription.

name: Ab wheel
sources: Strength Level - Ab Wheel Rollout standards (older snapshot) <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/ab-wheel-rollout> ; Strength Level - Ab Wheel Rollout (current table) <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/ab-wheel-rollout/lb> ; FitnessVolt - Ab wheel strength standards <https://fitnessvolt.com/strength-standards/ab-wheel-rollout/> ; AOL citing Brewer - ab wheel coaching targets <https://www.aol.com/why-ab-wheel-challenging-effective-130000654.html>
method: Median of three published figures at each tier: Strength Level older snapshot (int 6, adv 14), coaching guidance (beginner 3-6, int 8, adv 12-15), Strength Level/FitnessVolt current community table (int ~20-21, adv 39-44, elite 60). Median at intermediate = 8, advanced = 14. Beginner 4 from coaching midpoint, elite 25 set between coaching ceiling and the inflated community table (judgement, anchored on current band). Novice = round(0.67 x 4) = 3. Source spread is very large; the community calculators likely include partial-range reps.
check: Numbers sit sensibly near the pull-up anchor and the current band 1/5/10/18/25, and they keep order with the easier Hollow Body Rock and harder Dragon Flag (both outside this group). FLAG: the AOL/Brewer coaching URL returns 404, so it may be invented or dead and should not be cited. Without it the beginner tier and the low median rest on the older Strength Level snapshot plus judgement. The community tables (int ~21, adv ~39-44) likely count partial reps. Confidence stays low.

name: Abdominal Draw-In
sources: Marathon Handbook / AthleanX / Livestrong stomach vacuum guidance <https://marathonhandbook.com/stomach-vacuum-exercise/>
method: Coaching guidance compiled for the stomach vacuum (same drawing-in move): beginner 5-10 s, intermediate 10-20 s, advanced 30-60 s. Mapped beginner 10, intermediate 20, advanced 40, elite 60; novice = round(0.67 x 10) = 7. No clinical norms exist; only one source family, so low confidence.
check: Numbers kept, status changed from sourced to derived. The only source is stomach-vacuum guidance, which covers a different drill (breath held on the exhale). The abdominal draw-in is done while breathing normally, so these are borrowed values, not a citation. A max hold of a draw-in may not be a meaningful test.

name: Bear plank hold
method: Derived from High plank hold (itself derived from forearm plank anchor x1.2) with the easier-variant rule x1.2 (ceil, holds to 5 s), per the app's easierId chain. Elite value (390 s) exceeds a meaningful test length; consider capping at 300 s. No published norms for this exact hold.
check: High plank x1.2 follows the easierId chain. Bear plank stays above High plank (45/65/125/200/325) and above Reverse Plank at every tier. The researcher suggested capping elite at 300 s; I did not, because 300 would fall below High plank's elite of 325 and invert the variant order. If a cap is wanted, cap the whole high-plank family together.

name: Cat Plank
sources: Fitness norms for the plank exercise (Chase et al.) <https://digitalcommons.wku.edu/ijesab/vol8/iss2/14>
method: No norms found. Treated as equivalent in difficulty to the forearm plank anchor (37/55/105/165/270, holds to 5 s). Sanity check: Chase et al. college norms men 25th/50th/75th = 84/110/135 s are consistent with the intermediate tier.
check: The catalogue sets harderId = hf_99 Forearm Plank, so Cat Plank (a knees-hovering, upper-back-rounded hold) must score above the forearm plank anchor 37/55/105/165/270, not equal it. Applied the easier-variant rule x1.2, rounded to 5 s, and matched the High plank values for consistency.

name: Dynamic side plank
method: No rep norms found. Converted forearm plank anchor (37/55/105/165/270 s) to reps at ~4 s per controlled rep: 9/14/26/41/68. Reps are per set, tempo-based conversion, not a citation.
check: The easierId is hf_100 Side Plank, so the right parent is the McGill side plank anchor (15/30/60/90/120 s), not the forearm plank. A side plank holds about half as long, so the forearm-plank base inflates the reps. Converted at about 3 s per controlled hip-dip rep, per side: 5/10/20/30/40.

name: High plank hold
sources: Fitness norms for the plank exercise (Chase et al.) <https://digitalcommons.wku.edu/ijesab/vol8/iss2/14>
method: Straight-arm plank is easier than forearm plank (shorter lever): forearm plank anchor x1.2 ceil, holds to 5 s: 45/65/125/200/325. No separate norms; Chase et al. forearm norms used only as sanity check.
check: Forearm plank x1.2 fits a shorter-lever hold. Order holds: Bear plank (easier) is higher at every tier. Plank up-down uses reps, so no tier comparison applies. Note that ceil would make intermediate 130 instead of 125; the difference is minor.

name: Incline Plank With Alternate Floor Touch
method: Dynamic plank base (forearm plank / 4 s per rep = 9/14/26/41/68) x1.2 ceil for the incline (easier) variant.
check: The dynamic plank base x1.2 for the incline (easier) variant is applied correctly, and the tiers are strictly increasing.

name: Lateral plank walk
method: Dynamic plank base (forearm plank / 4 s per rep): 9/14/26/41/68. No norms found.
check: The dynamic plank base is a reasonable derivation, the tiers are strictly increasing, and the values are close to the current band 5/15/25/40/60.

name: Leg Wheel
method: Derived from Ab wheel (3/4/8/14/25) with the harder-variant rule /1.2 (rounded). No norms for this exact move.
check: Wrong parent. The catalogue describes Leg Wheel as lying supine and circling the raised legs, not as an ab-wheel variant. Its easierId is wger_1410 (Plank with Alternating Leg Lift, 9/14/26/41/68) and its harderId is Dragon Flag. Re-derived with the harder-variant rule (/1.2) from wger_1410, which keeps the required order.

name: Plank Jump-In
method: No norms. Dynamic plank base (forearm plank / 4 s per rep): 9/14/26/41/68. Possibly plyometric in execution; max-reps test is marginal.
check: Derived from the dynamic plank base, strictly increasing, and close to the current band 10/20/35/50/75. A plyometric jump-in has a faster cadence than 4 s per rep, so these may be conservative. The easier move, Bear plank, is a hold, so no order comparison applies.

name: Plank Reach
method: Dynamic plank base (forearm plank / 4 s per rep): 9/14/26/41/68. No norms found.
check: The dynamic plank base derivation is fine and the tiers are strictly increasing.

name: Plank up-down
method: Dynamic plank base 9/14/26/41/68 with harder-variant rule /1.2 (rounded) because of the repeated elbow-to-hand transitions. No norms found.
check: Base /1.2 for the elbow-to-hand transitions sits correctly below the other dynamic planks. Elite 57 is above the push-up elite of 36, but an up-down is a partial press and the plank-endurance limit dominates, so it is plausible.

name: Plank with Alternating Leg Lift
method: Dynamic plank base (forearm plank / 4 s per rep): 9/14/26/41/68. No norms found.
check: Derived from the dynamic plank base. Order holds: it scores above its harderId wger_1909 Leg Wheel (adjusted to 8/12/22/34/57) at every tier.

name: Plank-to-Elbow Extension
method: Same movement family as plank up-down: dynamic plank base /1.2 = 8/12/22/34/57. No norms found.
check: Same family as Plank up-down, using base /1.2. Consistent.

name: Reverse Plank
method: No reverse plank norms found (search returned only forward plank). Used forearm plank anchor 37/55/105/165/270 (holds to 5 s) as the closest parent; the app places the move between bear plank and its harder variant.
check: The forearm plank equivalent is a reasonable placement. Order holds: the easier Bear plank (55/80/150/240/390) is higher at every tier.

name: Scissor Kick
sources: FitnessVolt - Flutter kicks strength standards <https://fitnessvolt.com/strength-standards/flutter-kicks> ; Healthline - scissor kicks <https://www.healthline.com/health/scissor-kicks>
method: Single published modelled table (FitnessVolt flutter kicks, 180 lb male: novice 14, intermediate 67, advanced 140, elite 228), mapped novice -> beginner. Time window and counting method unstated (per leg vs per cycle can differ 2x); Healthline's 12-20 reps is a training dose, not a max. Only one numeric source, so low confidence and values are likely high versus the current band.
check: Spot-check of the FitnessVolt page confirms the 180 lb male figures (novice 14, int 67, adv 140, elite 228). It is a modelled estimate and does not say whether each leg counts as a rep. It is the only numeric source, and its 14 -> 67 step (4.8x) and elite 228 are implausible for one clean set. Healthline gives a training dose, not a max. Treated FitnessVolt intermediate 67 as the anchor value and placed the other tiers with hollow-hold ratios (10/20/45/60/90 relative to 45): 15/30/67/89/134.

name: Stomach Vacuum
sources: Marathon Handbook - stomach vacuum exercise <https://marathonhandbook.com/stomach-vacuum-exercise/>
method: Coaching guidance across several articles: beginner 5-10 s, intermediate 10-20 s, advanced 30-60 s. Mapped beginner 10, intermediate 20, advanced 40, elite 60; novice = round(0.67 x 10) = 7. No clinical norms.
check: Coaching guidance (beginner 5-10 s, intermediate 10-20 s, advanced 30-60 s) is mapped sensibly. The hold is limited by breath-holding, which is consistent with a short ceiling. It has only one source family, so confidence stays low.

name: Swimmers
sources: Strength Level - Superman standards <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/superman>
method: No swimmer norms found. Derived from the closest sourced move, Superman (Strength Level male: novice 8, intermediate 25-28, advanced 46-53, elite 81), mapped SL novice -> Aurora beginner 8, intermediate averaged 27, advanced 50, elite 81, novice round(0.67 x 8) = 5.
check: Superman reps from Strength Level are the closest proxy. The easierId hf_117 is Superman Hold, a hold measured in seconds, so the variant rule cannot be checked across units. Values are strictly increasing and close to the current band 10/20/35/50/75. Correctly marked as derived.

name: TRX roll out
method: Derived from Ab wheel (3/4/8/14/25) with the easier-variant rule x1.2 ceil, since TRX angle is adjustable. No norms for this exact move.
check: Ab wheel x1.2 for the adjustable-angle TRX rollout is applied correctly, and the tiers are strictly increasing. It has the same easier/harder neighbours as Ab wheel (Hollow Body Rock and Dragon Flag, outside this group).

name: 3/4 Sit-Up
sources: Sit-Ups (1-Min, Cooper): Males, Age 20-29 <https://fitnessnorms.pages.dev/strength/cooper-sit-ups/male/age-20-29> ; StrengthLevel Sit Ups standards <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/sit-ups/lb> ; StrengthLevel Crunches standards <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/crunches/lb>
method: Sit-up standards: median per tier of Cooper-labelled 1-min sit-up percentiles (men 20-29), StrengthLevel sit-ups (men), and StrengthLevel crunches (third source because sit-up sources differ 33% at intermediate). Percentile mapping: 20th=beginner, 50th=intermediate, 80th=advanced, 95th=elite. Applied to the 3/4 sit-up as the same family; novice = round(0.67 x beginner).
check: Variant order inverted: easierId hf_115 (Bicycle Crunch 8/12/40/75/120) must sit above at every tier, but the researcher's values were higher at novice, beginner and intermediate, and equal at advanced. Fixed with the harder-variant rule, bicycle / 1.2 (rounded). The sources are full sit-up norms (a 1-minute Cooper test and StrengthLevel sit-ups), not 3/4 sit-up norms, so this is effectively derived. Cooper URL spot-checked and the numbers match.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
sources: StrengthLevel Ab Wheel Rollout <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/ab-wheel-rollout> ; FitnessVolt Ab Wheel Rollout standards <https://fitnessvolt.com/strength-standards/ab-wheel-rollout/> ; AOL / Brewer coaching guidance on ab wheel <https://www.aol.com/why-ab-wheel-challenging-effective-130000654.html>
method: Community calculators (StrengthLevel, FitnessVolt) give about 5/21/41/65 but differ greatly from coaching guidance (Brewer: 3-6 beginner, ~8 intermediate, 12-15 advanced; FitnessVolt readiness rule 10 kneeling reps; mastery 12-15). Took the median of calculator, Brewer coaching and readiness figures per tier: beginner 5, intermediate 10, advanced 14. Elite extrapolated using the StrengthLevel elite/advanced ratio (about 1.6), giving 22. Novice = round(0.67 x 5).
check: Numbers kept: they sit plausibly near the pull-up anchor 3/4/8/13/18 for an advanced move. The AOL/Brewer coaching URL returned 404 on spot-check, so it is unverified and must be replaced or dropped. Confidence lowered to low, because only the calculators (StrengthLevel and FitnessVolt, about 5/20/40/62, likely kneeling) are verifiable and they are much higher.

name: Abdominal Crunch
sources: StrengthLevel Crunches <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/crunches/lb> ; Cooper 1-min sit-ups men 20-29 <https://fitnessnorms.pages.dev/strength/cooper-sit-ups/male/age-20-29>
method: Average per tier of StrengthLevel crunches (men; novice=20th) and Cooper-labelled 1-min sit-up percentiles (men 20-29) as the nearest published crunch-type test. Intermediate 41 vs 40 (2.5% spread). Avg beginner 23.5, advanced 61, elite 85.5, rounded; novice = round(0.67 x 24).
check: Two sources agree at intermediate (41 vs 40). Tiers increase and the curve is plausible. The Cooper source is a 1-minute sit-up test used as a proxy; noted.

name: Advanced Kettlebell Windmill
method: Loaded, technique-limited kettlebell lift; max reps depends on bell weight and is not a meaningful bodyweight max test.
check: Load-dependent kettlebell lift, not a bodyweight max test.

name: Air Bike
method: Air bike is the same movement as the bicycle crunch (opposite elbow to knee, legs cycling); copied from the sourced Bicycle Crunch (hf_115) standard.
check: Same movement as Bicycle Crunch, so it copies the kept bicycle standard.

name: Alternate Heel Touchers
method: No norms found. Short-range oblique side-reach, easier than a crunch: parent Abdominal Crunch (16/24/40/60/85) x1.2 (ceil, rounded), novice = round(0.67 x 29).
check: Crunch x 1.2 is a reasonable choice for an easier short-range move. Novice 19 vs strict ceil 20 is a trivial difference; kept. harderId toe_touchers is not in this group.

name: Arch Body Hold
sources: Biering-Sorensen young adult men (secondary summary) <https://orthofixar.com/?p=7871> ; Isometric back extensor endurance, Nigerian young adults <https://e-space.mmu.ac.uk/630030/1/Kuwait%20article.pdf> ; Normative study 561 adults 19-67 (via Physio-pedia/MMU) <https://www.physio-pedia.com/Biering-Sorenson_Test>
method: Closest published test is the Biering-Sorensen back-extensor hold (arms/legs not lifted, so only a proxy). Converted mean+SD to percentiles (20th = mean-0.84SD, 80th = +0.84SD, 95th = +1.65SD) for three samples: young men 146+/-51 s, Nigerian young adults 98+/-44 s, mixed adults 113+/-46 s. Spread at intermediate was 42%, so used the median per tier, rounded to 5 s; novice = round(0.67 x 75).
check: Status changed from sourced to derived (proxy): all sources measure the Biering-Sorensen bench hold, not a floor arch/superman hold. Numbers kept. They sit near the forearm plank anchor (37/55/105/165/270) and above the hollow hold (10/20/45/60/90), which fits the arch hold being the easier counterpart. Confidence low.

name: Bent Press
method: Loaded, highly technical kettlebell/barbell lift; rep max depends on external load, not a bodyweight max test.
check: Load-dependent technical lift, not a max test.

name: Bent-Knee Hip Raise
method: No direct norms. Floor reverse-crunch type hip raise is easier than the calibrated hanging knee raise anchor (3/8/12/15/20): anchor x1.2 (ceil).
check: Hanging knee raise x 1.2 (ceil) is applied correctly. Probably conservative for a floor reverse crunch, but rule-consistent.

name: Bent-knee Iron Cross
method: Lying knee-drop spinal twist is a mobility/stretch drill, not a meaningful max-reps test.
check: Mobility twist drill, not a max test.

name: Bicycle Crunch
sources: StrengthLevel Bicycle Crunch <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/bicycle-crunch> ; FitnessVolt Bicycle Crunch <https://fitnessvolt.com/strength-standards/bicycle-crunch>
method: Two calculators agree at intermediate (StrengthLevel 39, FitnessVolt 42; about 8% spread). Averaged intermediate 40; advanced averaged 71/84 = 78, trimmed to 75; beginner from FitnessVolt novice 10 plus StrengthLevel crunch ratio (14/41) giving 12; elite from FitnessVolt 132 and StrengthLevel ratio (116/41 x 40 = 113) giving about 120. Novice = round(0.67 x 12). Counts are total reps (both sides).
check: StrengthLevel spot-checked: Novice 14, Intermediate 39, Advanced 71, Elite 110 (the researcher omitted the novice and elite figures). Two-source averages: beginner (14+10)/2 = 12, intermediate 40.5, advanced 77.5, elite 121. These match the proposal. Kept as the parent of the sit-up family.

name: Bird Dog
method: Motor-control and stability drill (typically 8-12 slow reps per side); no norms found and max clean reps is not meaningful.
check: Motor-control drill; max reps not meaningful.

name: Black Widow Knee Slides
method: No norms found. Slider knee-tuck from plank is comparable in demand to the hanging knee raise anchor: parent hanging knee raise 3/8/12/15/20 x1.0.
check: Hanging knee raise anchor x 1.0 is plausible for a slider knee tuck. Low confidence.

name: Body Saw
method: No norms found. Slider/TRX plank saw is comparable to a rollout; parent Ab Wheel Rollout (hf_113) values used x1.0.
check: Copies Ab Wheel Rollout x 1.0; it shares the same easier/harder links (hf_103/hf_108). Low confidence.

name: Bottoms Up
method: No norms found. Lying hip-lift (reverse crunch) type: hanging knee raise anchor x1.2 (ceil).
check: Hanging knee raise x 1.2 (ceil), same as the hip-raise family.

name: Butt-Ups
method: No norms found. Same hip-lift movement as Bottoms Up / Bent-Knee Hip Raise: hanging knee raise anchor x1.2 (ceil).
check: Same hip-lift family; hanging knee raise x 1.2 (ceil).

name: Butterfly Sit Up
method: Butterfly (soles together) sit-up is slightly harder than a sit-up; parent 3/4 Sit-Up/sit-up sourced standard (17/25/41/75/116) / 1.2, rounded.
check: Variant order inverted: easierId hf_115 (Bicycle 8/12/40/75/120) was below the proposed 14/21 at novice and beginner. The parent 3/4 Sit-Up was also adjusted. Re-derived as the adjusted 3/4 Sit-Up (7/10/33/63/100) / 1.2, which now sits below both the bicycle and the 3/4 sit-up.

name: Cocoons
method: Crunch with simultaneous knee tuck, harder than a crunch: parent Abdominal Crunch (16/24/40/60/85) / 1.2, rounded.
check: Crunch / 1.2 applied correctly for a harder crunch variant.

name: Crab toe touch
method: No norms found. Dynamic abdominal-reach rep exercise of crunch-level difficulty: copied from sourced Abdominal Crunch standard.
check: Copies the crunch standard; low confidence but plausible.

name: Cross-Body Crunch
method: Crunch variant with rotation, equal difficulty; copied from sourced Abdominal Crunch standard (reps counted total).
check: Crunch variant at the same difficulty; copies the crunch standard.

name: Cross-body mountain climber
method: No published norms for continuous mountain climbers (searched; only an unquantified 2-min test). Treated as a harder dynamic plank: forearm plank anchor 37/55/105/165/270 s / 1.2, rounded to 5 s.
check: Hold-effort derivation from forearm plank / 1.2, rounded to 5 s, applied correctly. easierId hf_121 is not in this group.

name: Crunch - Hands Overhead
method: Longer lever makes it harder than a standard crunch: parent Abdominal Crunch (16/24/40/60/85) / 1.2, rounded.
check: A longer lever makes it harder: crunch / 1.2, applied correctly.

name: Crunches
sources: StrengthLevel Crunches <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/crunches/lb> ; Cooper 1-min sit-ups men 20-29 <https://fitnessnorms.pages.dev/strength/cooper-sit-ups/male/age-20-29>
method: Same as Abdominal Crunch: average per tier of StrengthLevel crunches and Cooper-labelled 1-min sit-up percentiles (men 20-29); intermediate 41 vs 40.
check: Same exercise and sources as Abdominal Crunch; values identical.

name: Crunches With Legs Up
method: Same trunk-flexion demand as a standard crunch with legs elevated; copied from sourced Abdominal Crunch standard.
check: Same flexion demand as a crunch; copies the crunch standard.

name: Decline Bench Leg Raise
method: Easier variant of hanging knee raise (calibrated anchor 3/8/12/15/20): parent x1.2 ceil.
check: Derived as easier than hanging knee raise (its harderId): HKR 3/8/12/15/20 x1.2 ceil. Strictly above HKR at every tier. In practice a decline leg raise is a bit harder than the flat lying leg raise, but no easier/harder link ties the two, so the numbers stay as they are.

name: Double Kettlebell Windmill
method: Load- and mobility-dependent skill drill; max clean reps is not a meaningful test.
check: Loaded mobility/skill drill; max reps depends on bell weight. Correctly not_max_test.

name: Double-Leg Abdominal Press
method: No norms found. Treated as a lying knee-tuck/leg-raise class move, so same as easier-than-hanging-knee-raise: anchor x1.2 ceil.
check: No norms. Lying leg-raise-class move set to HKR x1.2 ceil, which is plausible and strictly increasing.

name: Dragon Flag
sources: BoxRox / Breaking Muscle dragon flag progressions (via search summary) <https://www.boxrox.com/dragon-flag-benefits-how-to-muscles-progressions/>
method: No numeric tier tables found. Coaching sources use 3x5 clean reps as the criterion to master a stage, with 5-10 clean reps per stage. Treated 5 clean reps of the full flag as roughly advanced to elite and placed lower tiers beneath; kept near the existing band.
check: Derived, not sourced: the source gives a 3x5 progression criterion, not tier norms. 1/2/4/7/10 is close to the current 1/2/4/8/12 and sits well below the hollow-rock family. Plausible.

name: Dynamic side hold
method: Treated as a side-plank class hold; used side plank McGill anchor 15/30/60/90/120.
check: Hold. Uses the side plank McGill anchor 15/30/60/90/120 directly. Reasonable for a side-plank class hold.

name: Elbow to Knee
sources: Sit-Ups (1-Min, Cooper) males 20-29 <https://fitnessnorms.pages.dev/strength/cooper-sit-ups/male/age-20-29>
method: Crunch-class move; used 1-minute sit-up norm (men 20-29) as parent: 20th pct 33, median 40, 80th 47, 95th 55; novice = round(0.67 x 33).
check: Crunch-class move mapped to the 1-minute sit-up percentiles (20th/50th/80th/95th = 33/40/47/55) with the standard novice rule. The source is a sit-up norm used as the parent, so the derived status is correct.

name: Flat Bench Leg Pull-In
method: Lying knee tuck, easier than hanging knee raise anchor: x1.2 ceil.
check: Easier than HKR (its harderId): 3/8/12/15/20 x1.2 ceil = 4/10/15/18/24. Order holds.

name: Flat Bench Lying Leg Raise
method: Lying straight-leg raise, slightly harder than the pull-in (about x0.9 of the pull-in values); still easier than hanging knee raise anchor.
check: Variant order broken: harderId is hanging_knee_raise (novice 3), and the proposed novice of 3 is not strictly above it. Raised novice to 4 (HKR 3 x1.2 ceil). The other tiers are already above HKR and unchanged.

name: Floor windshield wiper
method: No norms found. Placed at hanging knee raise anchor level (3/8/12/15/20) as a mid-ladder move between easier hf_122 and harder hf_111; deliberately not chained from the sourced hanging leg raise, which looks inflated.

sources: StrengthLevel inverted row standards <https://strengthlevel.com/strength-standards/inverted-row> ; FitnessVolt inverted row standards <https://fitnessvolt.com/strength-standards/inverted-row>
method: StrengthLevel (men, 180 lb reference) 8/19/32/46 and FitnessVolt 7/19/33/48 for novice/intermediate/advanced/elite. Both are lifter-population tables. I mapped their novice to Aurora beginner. Averaged: beginner 8, intermediate 19, advanced 33, elite 47. Aurora novice = round(0.67 x 8) = 5.
check: Sources verified. StrengthLevel male novice/intermediate/advanced/elite is 8/19/32/46, and FitnessVolt agrees within about 5%. Mapping source novice to Aurora beginner follows the Endura rule, and Aurora novice = round(0.67 x 8) = 5. It sits between Ring Row (easier) and Wide-Grip Inverted Row (harder) correctly. The two sources may not be independent.

name: One-Arm Inverted Row
method: Derived from Wide-Grip Inverted Row (itself Inverted Row / 1.2) divided by 1.2 again, following the harder-variant chain easier=hf_40. Reps per arm.
check: The researcher's 3/6/13/23/33 is far above pull-up (its harderId), and 33 reps per arm at elite is implausible. The easier move must score higher than the harder one, so the values must sit above pull-up 3/4/8/13/18 and below Wide-Grip Inverted Row 4/7/16/28/39. I used pull-up x1.2 (ceil) = 4/5/10/16/22, but novice 4 would tie Wide-Grip Inverted Row. I set novice to 3 instead, which ties pull-up; no whole number fits between 3 and 4. Reps per arm.

name: Pull-up Isometric Hold
sources: Topend Sports Bent-Arm Hang (Eurofit) calculator <https://www.topendsports.com/testing/tests/bent-arm-hang-eurofit.htm> ; Fitnessnorms Bent-Arm Hang males age 16 <https://fitnessnorms.pages.dev/strength/bent-arm-hang/male/age-16/> ; Topend Sports Flexed-Arm Hang (Marine-style table) <https://www.topendsports.com/testing/tests/flexed-arm-hang-ipft.htm>
method: Mapped to flexed-arm-hang (chin over bar) norms. Three sources were far apart at the intermediate tier. Eurofit age-16 male median is about 22 s. A Marine-style table has good 30-49 s and excellent 50+ s. The Eurofit-based adult calculator has good 45 s and excellent 70 s. The median per tier is intermediate 30, advanced 45, elite 65. Beginner 15 and novice 10 are about 0.67 x. A fourth calculator (above average 9-13 s) is an outlier and was excluded. Rounded to 5 s.
check: Fitnessnorms figures verified: 50th percentile 21.75 s, 75th 35.86 s, 95th 66.71 s. Taking the median across the 3 sources and rounding to 5 s is reasonable, and the values sit below the dead hang anchor 15/30/60/90/120. Mapping caveat: the researcher put the 75th percentile at advanced, while the percentile rule puts about the 80th at advanced. The difference is small. Low confidence: the main source is youth data and the spread is 35%.
